findings.reason: The original standalone tile contains no illustration. A configuration graph materially clarifies the reduction by distinguishing machine transitions from the fresh-target arcs. A concrete constant-workspace machine instance avoids implying that a generic NL computation has this particular branching structure.
findings.action: Appended final Remarks defining a five-configuration toy machine and drawing its reachable graph plus the fresh target, with solid legal-transition arrows and dashed accepting-to-target arrows.

correction: Added a mathematically specified configuration-graph instance in final Remarks; original title, statement, proof and all frontmatter preserved exactly.

diagram_math_checks.result: For each fixed input x, the toy machine leaves tapes and heads unchanged and has five reachable configurations s_x,c_x,r_x,a_x,b_x distinguished by finite control state. Its nondeterministic transitions are exactly s_x→c_x, s_x→r_x, c_x→a_x and c_x→b_x; a_x,b_x are accepting halts and r_x is a rejecting halt. This is a fixed constant-workspace machine, consistent with def-l-and-nl and the configuration description in lem-logspace-machines-have-polynomially-many-configurations proof step 1.1.

Item proof step 1.2 adds a fresh vertex t_x and one arc from every accepting configuration. Thus a_x→t_x and b_x→t_x are precisely the two dashed added arcs. No target arc leaves r_x or a nonaccepting configuration. All six arcs have endpoints among the displayed six vertices; t_x is distinct from all five machine configurations.

Independent enumeration of the stated six-edge adjacency data gives exactly s_x,c_x,a_x,t_x and s_x,c_x,b_x,t_x as directed s_x-to-t_x paths. Removing their final added arcs gives the two accepting machine branches, as in item proof step 3.1. The rejecting branch s_x,r_x cannot reach t_x.

Original-resolution native preview inspected: six vertices and six arrows visible, four solid transitions oriented away from s_x then c_x, two dashed arrows oriented from a_x,b_x into t_x. In/out degrees are s:(0,2), c:(1,2), a:(1,1), b:(1,1), r:(1,0), t:(2,0). Every source edge is present; this acyclic graph has no intended closing edge or cycle. No clipping or label overlap affects the diagram.
The original complete proof is preserved byte-for-byte; the appended Remarks explicitly state that it is independent of the figure. No statement or dependency change is needed.
